## 1. Traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 1**
- **Guzik (Calvary Chapel):** Everything is now in order, both practical (wall, doors, gatekeepers) and spiritual (singers, Levites). The walls were rebuilt so the people could worship God more freely, not just to have walls to look at. He applies this: every victory should lead us into deeper praise. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-7/
- **Commentators disagree about what the Levites were "appointed" to do:**
  - **Keil & Delitzsch:** They were put in charge of watching the walls and gates. This was unusual, because normally only the gatekeepers guarded the temple, and the singers and Levites didn't keep watch at all. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
  - **Ellicott:** They were probably put in charge of all the walls. He calls this an extraordinary step, explained by these organised groups making up a large share of the city's people. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
  - **Pulpit Commentary:** Priests and Levites were nearly half of Jerusalem's population, and Levites had always guarded the temple gates. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/nehemiah/7.htm
  - **Gill:** The opposite view. They weren't posted at the wall gates; they went back to temple service after helping with the building. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
  - **Benson:** Nehemiah gave orders for the Levites to be called in for the wall's dedication (Neh 12:27). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
  - **Matthew Henry:** Offers both options: their general temple work, which had been neglected and was now revived, or getting ready for the dedication. Either way, God's worship defends a place, and ministers who do their duty are "watchmen on the walls" (Isa 62:6). https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Neh/Neh_007.cfm
  - **Steven Cole:** Most commentators say these men also guarded the gates. He agrees with Derek Kidner that they are listed first because worship was the city's reason for existing. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-7-counting-god-nehemiah-71-73

**v. 2**
- **Who is "he"?** Barnes, Poole, Gill and the Cambridge Bible all say "faithful man" describes Hananiah. Poole and Gill add that Hanani needed no praise, since his trip to Susa (Neh 1) had already shown his zeal. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-2.htm
- **Why Hananiah was trusted:**
  - **Poole and JFB:** His fear of God was why he was faithful. Nehemiah trusted it to protect him from temptations to betray the city once Nehemiah left. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-2.htm
  - **Gill:** Hananiah's godliness had few equals. Gill also notes Jarchi's alternative reading: he had feared God "of many days," that is, for a long time. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-2.htm
  - **Keil & Delitzsch:** The Hebrew makes a comparison: "more God-fearing than many." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
- **His post:**
  - **Ellicott:** "Ruler of the palace" means commander of the fortress (Neh 2:8). He served the Persian king, but his piety was what recommended him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
  - **Cambridge:** Probably commanded troops keeping order in the city. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-2.htm
  - **Pulpit and Cambridge:** The two appointees match the two "rulers of half the district" in Neh 3:9, 12. Pulpit calls this an "undesigned coincidence." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/nehemiah/7.htm
- **Nehemiah leaving:** Gill, JFB and Matthew Henry suppose Nehemiah was about to go back to Persia and left these men in charge. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-2.htm ; https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Neh/Neh_007.cfm
- **Benson:** Nehemiah didn't pick officers out of favouritism toward relatives or friends, but for their godliness and fitness. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
- **Application:**
  - **Guzik:** Nehemiah wasn't after political glory and could let the work go. People without special gifts can still be greatly used if they are faithful and fear God. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-7/
  - **Cole:** Hanani was the civil leader and Hananiah the military leader. The Hebrew for "faithful" means reliable, truthful and firm, and godly character is the main requirement for leaders. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-7-counting-god-nehemiah-71-73
  - **Matthew Henry:** Some who fear God fear him more than others. True fear of God shows itself in faithfulness to everyone. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Neh/Neh_007.cfm

**v. 3**
- **"Until the sun is hot":**
  - **JFB and Barnes:** Eastern gates were normally opened at sunrise, so this was an unusual precaution while enemies were plotting. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-3.htm
  - **Poole and Benson:** Wait for full daylight, so approaching enemies can be seen and the townspeople are up and ready. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-3.htm
  - **Pulpit:** Somewhere between sunrise and noon. Dathe's "before noon" goes too far. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/nehemiah/7.htm
  - **Cambridge:** Rashi's "until mid-day" is wrong. Shutting the gates was a sign of suspicion, the opposite of the peace pictured in Isa 60:11. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-3.htm
- **"While they stand by":**
  - **Gill:** Mentions the view of Aben Ezra and Grotius that Hanani and Hananiah were to be present, but thinks the appointed watchmen are meant. They were to handle the doors themselves to check they were fast. Only residents, not foreigners, were to keep watch, each near his own house so he would be more careful. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-3.htm
  - **Cambridge:** The two officers couldn't possibly be at every gate. The Levite guard had to be on duty while the doors were secured. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-3.htm
  - **Keil & Delitzsch:** The gates were to be occupied before daybreak, opened only when the watch was in place, and closed before the watch left. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-3.htm
- **Application:**
  - **Guzik:** The gates opened late and closed early because security was tight. Walls don't guard themselves, and victories in the Christian life are often lost for lack of a guard. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-7/
  - **Matthew Henry (Concise):** Public safety depends on each person guarding himself and his family against sin. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-3.htm
  - **Cole:** Nehemiah trusted God but also posted a guard (cf. 4:9). https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-7-counting-god-nehemiah-71-73

**v. 4**
- **What "large and spacious" means:** Keil & Delitzsch, Cambridge and Pulpit all say the Hebrew is literally "broad on both sides / every way." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-4.htm
- **"Houses not rebuilt" isn't literal:**
  - **Keil & Delitzsch:** People had lived there for ninety years; there just weren't enough houses for the city's size. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-4.htm
  - **Cambridge and Pulpit:** It means large empty spaces inside the walls. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-4.htm
  - **JFB:** Houses were spread out with gardens between them, and most were crude sheds or loose-stone huts. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-4.htm
  - **Poole:** Only makeshift buildings of boards or stones. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-4.htm
- **Why the people were few:**
  - **Gill:** The wall followed the old foundations. Many returnees chose to live in country towns because Jerusalem was so desolate. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-4.htm
  - **Barnes:** Only 42,360 came with Zerubbabel and fewer than 2,000 with Ezra. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-4.htm
- **Matthew Henry:** Nehemiah walled the city "in faith," relying on the promise in Zech 8 that it would be filled again. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Neh/Neh_007.cfm
- **Guzik:** Nehemiah wanted to see how he could bless the people now that the walls were finished. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-7/

**v. 5**
- **"My God put it into my heart":**
  - **Poole, JFB and Benson:** Even a prudent, common-sense plan is credited to God's grace directing him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-5.htm ; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-7.htm
  - **Gill:** Nehemiah credited every good idea to God (2 Cor 3:5). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-5.htm
- **Purpose of the census:**
  - **Pulpit:** Nehemiah saw it as divine inspiration. A census would prepare for moving country people into the capital, and, following Jewish custom, it was by family line. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/nehemiah/7.htm ; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/nehemiah-7.html
  - **Cambridge:** Points to Neh 11:1–3 as the result. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-5.htm
  - **Gill:** It would also preserve family records, so that the Messiah's descent could be clearly known. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-5.htm
  - **JFB:** A key aim was to confirm who was legally entitled to serve at the altar. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-7.htm
- **Guzik:** As with his night inspection of the walls (2:11–16), Nehemiah first needed to know his situation, so he went to the earlier register (Ezra 2). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-7/
- **Matthew Henry (Concise):** Under God, a city's safety depends more on its people than on its walls. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-5.htm

**vv. 6–7**
- **Whose list this is:** Constable says it records those who came back in 537 BC with Sheshbazzar, Zerubbabel and Jeshua, not Nehemiah's companions. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/7-7.html
- **The "Nehemiah" in v. 7:** A preceptaustin note says he isn't the cupbearer but an earlier leader born in exile. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezra-2-commentary
- **Name differences from Ezra 2:2:**
  - **Pulpit:** Nehemiah adds a sixth name, Nahamani, to Ezra's eleven, and spells some names differently (Azariah/Seraiah, Raamiah/Reelaiah, Mispereth/Mizpar, Nehum/Rehum). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/nehemiah/7.htm
  - **Cambridge and the Geneva notes:** Give the same equivalences. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-7.htm
  - **Preceptaustin's Ezra 2 notes:** Most scholars think a copyist dropped a name in Ezra, and that twelve leaders stand for the twelve tribes. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezra-2-commentary
- **Guzik:** Only about 2% of the exiles came back. These "pioneers" are named twice in Scripture because they left comfort to answer God's call. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-7/
- **Matthew Henry:** The list is essentially the same as Ezra 2. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Neh/Neh_007.cfm

**vv. 8–24 (family counts)**
I found no notes on individual families. These general points apply to the whole list:
- **Why the numbers differ from Ezra 2:**
  - **Gill:** Ezra's list was drawn up in Babylon, Nehemiah's after arrival. Some people dropped out or died on the way, others joined later, and name differences come from copyists, pronunciation, or men having two names. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-7.htm
  - **JFB:** Similar. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-7.htm
  - **Clarke (Methodist):** Families had died out or arrived since, so Nehemiah updated parts of the list. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/nehemiah/7-7.html
  - **GotQuestions:** Ezra's family figures add up to 29,818 and Nehemiah's to 31,089. The likelier explanation is the different times and places the lists were made, including families growing. https://www.gotquestions.org/Ezra-Nehemiah-numbers.html
  - **Pulpit:** Disagrees. Both books give the same grand total (42,360), which tells against Bishop Patrick's "Babylon list vs. Jerusalem list" theory. Pulpit thinks copying errors are more likely: a faded number-sign makes a copyist lower a figure by one, ten, a hundred and so on. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/nehemiah-7.html ; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/nehemiah/7.htm
  - **Preceptaustin:** Hebrew numbers in lists were hard to copy. Inerrancy applies to the original manuscripts, so some copying differences may simply not be resolvable. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-7-commentary
- **Application:**
  - **Cole:** The list shows that individuals matter to God, who knows his people by name (John 10:3), and that families matter. https://www.preceptaustin.org/nehemiah-7-commentary
  - **Guzik:** Nothing about God's people is too small to be recorded. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/nehemiah-7/

## 2. Differences between Protestant traditions
I found no real split along denominational lines. The sources include Gill (Baptist), Matthew Henry and Geneva (Reformed), Benson and Clarke (Methodist), Pulpit and Ellicott (Anglican), Keil & Delitzsch (Lutheran scholars) and Guzik (Calvary Chapel). They differ on details, not by tradition:
- whether the Levites guarded the walls (v. 1), and
- why the numbers differ (vv. 8–24): Gill, Clarke and GotQuestions say different times and places, while Pulpit and preceptaustin say copying errors.

## 3. Other views
- **v. 1:** The Cambridge Bible notes that Sirach 49:13, a book Catholics and Orthodox count as Scripture, praises Nehemiah for raising the walls and setting up the gates and bars. It also comments that Nehemiah's trust in the Levites suggests they backed his plan for a religious community that would shut out Samaritans and foreigners. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/nehemiah/7-1.htm
- I found nothing on modern-scholarship, Catholic/Orthodox or prosperity/word-of-faith readings of vv. 1–24.
